title: Queue-Batching Interaction Prober for Multi-Profile Workloads
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: Build a reproducible prober/harness that quantifies how continuous batching and in-queue amplification interact under mixed request profiles (short chat messages, long-context completions, and embeddings). We need fine-grained signals (tokens/sec, per-request p50/p95/p99, queue depth distribution, batch sizes, and KV-cache hit rate) to surface regimes where queueing causes pathological tail amplification. Deliverables: (1) harness code and config templates for multi-profile synthetic arrival processes, (2) dashboards and automated regression checks, (3) guidance for routing/threshold tuning to bound tail risk.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay at least three workload mixes (chat-heavy, long-completion-heavy, embedding-bursty) with configurable poisson/bursty arrival params
Collects and stores per-request: tokens_generated, wall_time_ms, queue_wait_ms, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (bool), model_variant in a time-series store
Detects regressions of p95 latency at 95% confidence using a maintained baseline and alerts when p95 degrades >10% for two consecutive runs
Dashboard shows heatmap of batch_size vs queue_wait percentile and a tokens/sec surface across offered load
Runbook entry created with recommended mitigations (batch caps, admission control, fallback variants) and at least one small-scale canary demonstrating a mitigation
test_plan: Implement arrival generator supporting: Poisson, Bimodal microburst, and periodic spike patterns; per-tenant profile weights
Profiler will exercise three model classes concurrently (chat-16k, completion-64k, embedding-large) to simulate heterogeneous resource footprints
Measure and record: offered_tps, accepted_tps, tokens_per_second, p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), queue_wait_ms, batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate
Two-stage regression detection: (A) offline statistical compare-to-baseline (bootstrap CI) for scheduled nightly runs and (B) online EWMA/CUSUM detector for CI during ramp tests
Stress matrix: sweep offered_tps from 10% to 150% of nominal capacity with concurrency scaling and capture phase transitions (queue growth vs steady-state batching efficiency)
instrumentation: In-harness tagging of each request with synthetic_profile, tenant_id, and request_size_tokens
Emit per-request JSON to kafka topic 'bench-requests' and aggregate into TimescaleDB for long-term analysis
Tracing integration: inject trace IDs to correlate queue wait and kernel scheduling spans (aws-xray compatible)
Expose derived metrics via Prometheus: bench_tokens_per_sec, bench_p95_latency_ms, bench_queue_depth, bench_batch_size_avg
Dashboards: Grafana panel 'Queue-Batching Interaction' and a heatmap panel for batch_size vs queue_wait_ms percentiles
related_prs: GH#218 - emit per-request telemetry to kafka topic bench-requests
